titre: The Hollywood blacklist began before McCarthyism
accroche: The hunt for communists in American film is associated with Senator McCarthy. It began more than two years before his Wheeling speech.
contenu_vulgarise:
In October 1947, ten Hollywood screenwriters, directors, and producers refuse to answer a single question before a congressional committee: are they, or have they ever been, members of the Communist Party. The senator whose name would later give this whole period its label, Joseph McCarthy, is not on that committee, and would not deliver his Wheeling speech until February 1950, more than two years later.

## A House vote, then a hotel lunch

In October 1947, the House Un-American Activities Committee (HUAC), a committee of the House of Representatives, holds nine days of hearings on supposed communist influence in the movie industry; forty-three people are summoned to Washington, and ten of them refuse to answer: Alvah Bessie, Herbert Biberman, Lester Cole, Edward Dmytryk, Ring Lardner Jr., John Howard Lawson, Albert Maltz, Samuel Ornitz, Adrian Scott, and Dalton Trumbo. On November 24, 1947, the House of Representatives votes 346 to 17 to cite them for contempt of Congress.

The next day, November 25, 1947, forty-eight film industry executives meeting behind closed doors at the Waldorf-Astoria Hotel in New York issue a joint statement, the Waldorf Statement, made public by Motion Picture Association president Eric Johnston. The ten will be fired or suspended without pay, and will not be rehired until they have cleared themselves of contempt and sworn that they are not communists; the signatories add that they will not knowingly employ a communist. Wikipedia dates the first Hollywood blacklist to that day.

The trials follow. Lawson goes first, from April 12 to 19, 1948, then Trumbo, from May 3 to 5, 1948. The other eight are tried in June 1950, without a jury, on the basis of the records of the first two trials. Eight of the ten are sentenced to one year in prison and a $1,000 fine; Biberman and Dmytryk, to six months and $500. Lawson and Trumbo enter prison on June 9, 1950, the other eight after their June 1950 sentencing. More than three hundred artists will subsequently be boycotted by the studios, according to Wikipedia.

## What this changes

Senator Joseph McCarthy delivers his Wheeling speech, in West Virginia, on February 9, 1950, claiming that the State Department is infested with communists. That speech is often presented as the starting point of the period that bears his name, McCarthyism. It comes more than two years after the House vote against the Hollywood Ten and the Waldorf Statement, by which the blacklist was already in force. McCarthy, a senator from Wisconsin since January 1947, sits in the Senate, a chamber distinct from the House of Representatives, where HUAC sits. The two episodes, often merged into a single story under one name, belong to two different institutions and two chronologies that only partly overlap: the machinery that broke the careers of the Hollywood Ten was already running before McCarthy gave his speech.

repere.texte: The House of Representatives votes to cite the Hollywood Ten for contempt of Congress on November 24, 1947, by 346 to 17; the Waldorf Statement establishing the first blacklist is published the next day. Senator McCarthy, often associated with the start of this communist hunt, did not deliver his Wheeling speech until February 9, 1950, more than two years later.

carte.punch: The Hollywood blacklist began more than two years before McCarthy's Wheeling speech.
carte.idee: The hunt for communists in Hollywood is associated with Senator Joseph McCarthy. But the House cites ten film professionals for contempt on November 24, 1947, and the studios' blacklist follows the next day: McCarthy did not deliver his Wheeling speech until February 1950.

quiz.question: What set up the mechanism of the Hollywood blacklist, and when?
choix: Senator McCarthy's first accusatory speech at Wheeling, in February 1950
The House of Representatives vote, followed by the studios' Waldorf Statement, in November 1947
The creation of the House Un-American Activities Committee, as early as 1938
The publication of the pamphlet Red Channels, which lists artists, in June 1950
quiz.explication: The first Hollywood blacklist was born of the Waldorf Statement of November 25, 1947, published the day after the November 24 House vote citing the ten for contempt. McCarthy's speech and the Red Channels pamphlet (June 1950) came more than two years later; HUAC, created in 1938, did not by itself establish the studios' list.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Which famous question do the Hollywood Ten refuse to answer before HUAC in 1947?
choix: Whether they met Soviet agents during the war
Whether they are, or have ever been, members of the Communist Party
Whether they inserted hidden propaganda into their films
Whether they traveled to the Soviet Union before the war
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The ten refuse to answer the question of whether they are, or have ever been, members of the Communist Party.

quiz_supplementaire.question: To which institution does Senator Joseph McCarthy belong, as opposed to the House Un-American Activities Committee, which held hearings on Hollywood in 1947?
choix: He also sits on HUAC, in the House of Representatives
He sits in the Senate, a chamber distinct from the House of Representatives, where HUAC sits
He heads the FBI, which oversees both the Senate and the House
He is a Supreme Court justice at the time of the hearings
quiz_supplementaire.explication: McCarthy has been a senator from Wisconsin since January 1947: he sits in the Senate, a chamber distinct from the House of Representatives, where the House Un-American Activities Committee, which held hearings on Hollywood in 1947, sits.
